venue.name: Rathtrevor Beach Nature House
venue.description: The Rathtrevor Beach Nature House is a small building inside Rathtrevor Beach Park at Parksville, run by Discover Parks, a project of the BC Parks Foundation. It reopened in the summer of 2023 for the first time since September 2019, and Discover Parks now lists it as closed again with a note saying see you in Summer 2027. Through the summer it is the meeting point for free drop-in programmes run by Discover Parks Ambassadors: a guided nature walk, a children's programme called Jerry's Rangers, and a Saturday evening presentation in the field behind the building. The park around it has a 2 km sandy beach, 5.5 km of easy walking trails, a playground, a large day-use and picnicking area, drinking water and toilets.

facility_notes.washrooms: The park's facility list includes drinking water, a playground, picnic areas, picnic shelters and pit or flush toilets.
facility_notes.lunch_space: The park also has a large day-use and picnicking area. Nothing says whether a group may use the Nature House itself.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Campsites, shower stalls, flush toilets, beach access, many walking trails, and parking stalls in the day-use area are all wheelchair-accessible. An accessible beach mat (mobi-mat) is available in the summer months to support beach access.

restrictions: Pets are not allowed in the sandy day-use area along the park's east shore, at any time of year.
Leashed pets are allowed on the north part of the beach next to the campground between May 1 and February 14.
There are no lifeguards on duty in BC Parks.
For your own safety and the preservation of the park, please obey all posted signs and keep to designated trails.
venue.hours_notes: The free drop-in programmes run in the park six days a week from June 13 to August 23. Nature walks are at 11:00 on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Jerry's Rangers is at 14:00 every day except Wednesday. The evening presentation is on Saturdays at 19:00. No opening hours are published for the Nature House building itself.
venue.seasonal_notes: Discover Parks lists the Rathtrevor Beach Nature House as now closed, with a line saying see you in Summer 2027. The summer programmes that meet outside the building finished on August 23, so nothing is running here at the moment. The park itself stays open year round and is busy through the summer.
venue.price_year_or_season: The programmes are free. The season published for them, June 13 to August 23, has already finished, and no other year is printed on the page.

programs.name: Guided nature walk
programs.description: A free guided walk along the park's designated trails with a Discover Parks Ambassador, meeting at the Nature House. Discover Parks describes it as a moderate-paced exploration with stops to learn about the park's features, lasting about an hour. It is rated easy, capped at 25 people, and walk-ins are welcome, so there is nothing to book. It ran at 11:00 on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday through the summer season, June 13 to August 23. Dogs are not allowed on the programme. The Nature House is the meeting point, reached by trail from parking lot 1, from the campground, or from the beach, and by a short trail between campsites 53 and 56.
programs.what_children_do: Walk with an Ambassador in an orange shirt along the park's marked trails for about an hour, stopping where the Ambassador points things out about the park.
programs.our_note: It is a full hour on the move with nowhere to sit down, so bring water and think about whether your youngest can manage that. Nobody takes a booking for it, which also means nobody is holding room for a group of twenty against a cap of twenty five. Ring the park operator before you drive out, because the season printed on their page has already finished.
programs.practical_summary: You meet at the Nature House, which is reached on foot by trail from car park one, from the campground or from the beach. The park has toilets, drinking water, picnic areas and picnic shelters. It is outdoors the whole way and no wet weather alternative is published.
programs.evidence: Please bring water and anything else you will need to keep yourself comfortable for being out and active for an hour.

programs.name: Jerry's Rangers
programs.description: A free children's programme run by Discover Parks Ambassadors, meeting at the Nature House. Discover Parks describes it as designed for kids aged 5 to 12 and says it teaches the importance of conservation, responsible recreation, Indigenous culture and outdoor safety in BC's parks. It ran at 14:00 every day except Wednesday through the summer season, June 13 to August 23, capped at 25 people, with walk-ins welcome and nothing to book. Dogs are not allowed. Nothing is published about how long a session lasts or what the children handle or make.
programs.our_note: The published age band starts at five, so this is not written for a preschool room. Nothing anywhere says how long a session runs, which is the first thing to ask. There is no phone number or email for it either, so twenty children turning up unannounced against a cap of twenty five is a gamble.
programs.practical_summary: It meets at the Nature House, reached on foot by trail from car park one, from the campground or from the beach. The park has toilets, drinking water, picnic areas and picnic shelters. Nothing says whether it moves under cover if it rains.
programs.evidence: This fun and educational program, designed for kids aged 5 to 12, teaches the importance of conservation, responsible recreation, Indigenous culture, and outdoor safety

programs.name: Evening presentation in the Old Farm Field
programs.description: A free evening session run by Discover Parks Ambassadors in the Old Farm Field, a large grassy area behind the Nature House reached by a short trail. Discover Parks calls it an interactive experience suitable for all ages and gives a bear safety talk and park jeopardy as examples of what it might be. It ran on Saturdays at 19:00 through the summer season, June 13 to August 23, capped at 25 people, with walk-ins welcome and nothing to book. Look for the Ambassadors and their large orange tent in the field between the walk-in tenting sites and the beachside playground. Dogs are not allowed.
programs.what_children_do: Gather in a grassy field beside a large orange tent while an Ambassador runs a talk or a quiz game about the park, such as bear safety or park jeopardy.
programs.our_note: A 7pm start puts this outside a daycare day, so it really suits a family outing or a group already camping in the park. It is out in the open with nothing overhead, so the weather decides it. The beachside playground is right next to the meeting spot if attention runs out.
programs.practical_summary: It happens outdoors in a grassy field behind the Nature House, reached by a short trail. The park has toilets, drinking water, picnic areas and picnic shelters. Nothing is published about a wet weather alternative.
programs.evidence: This is an exciting and interactive experience in your park, perfect for all ages!

OPERATOR. The tracker website, naturehouse.ca, redirects to discoverparks.ca. This Nature House is run by Discover Parks, a project of the BC Parks Foundation, the same operator as the Goldstream and Miracle Beach nature houses already in this catalog. Everything recorded here was read from Rathtrevor's own section, its own park page and its own activity page. Nothing has been carried across from the other two, and the free entry and free activities line that appears on the shared nature house page belongs to the Miracle Beach section, not this one, so no admission price has been recorded here.

THE BUILDING IS CLOSED. Discover Parks lists the Rathtrevor Beach Nature House as now closed with a note saying see you in Summer 2027. Nothing on the site describes what is inside it, so no visit to the building has been recorded as a programme. Do not plan an indoor stop here without checking first.

NO ACTIVITY PAGE FOR THE BUILDING. Unlike Goldstream and Miracle Beach, Rathtrevor has no Visit the Heart of the Park page on the operator's site. Seven likely addresses following the pattern used for the other two nature houses were tried in a browser on 2026-09-10 and every one returned 404, while the equivalent Goldstream and Miracle Beach addresses returned 200 in the same run. The only Rathtrevor activity page that exists is the free drop-in programmes one used here.

THE OPERATOR'S OWN ACTIVITY SEARCH IS BROKEN. Their Things to Do search returns Sorry, no results found for Rathtrevor Beach Park and also for no filter at all, so a director browsing their site normally would conclude there is nothing on here. The Things to Do panel on the Rathtrevor park page renders empty for the same reason. The programme page was reached through the Discover Parks Ambassadors page instead.

NO GROUP OR SCHOOL PROGRAMME IS PUBLISHED. Nothing on the operator's site or on the BC Parks page for this park mentions school groups, daycares or booked group visits. The BC Parks page for Rathtrevor, unlike the one for Goldstream, gives no Nature House email and no group contact. Whether groups are taken is unanswered rather than a no.

NO BOOKING ROUTE AT ALL. No email, phone number or form is published for the Nature House or for these programmes. They are marked as not bookable and walk-ins welcome. The park operator named on the BC Parks page is RLC Park Services at office@rlcparks.ca and 1-250-474-1336, but that is the campground and day-use operator rather than the Nature House, so it has not been recorded as the booking route. The Hosted By panel on the programme page renders a heading with no host name under it.
NO STREET ADDRESS is published for the Nature House or for the park. BC Parks says only that the park is 3 km south of Parksville on Highway 19A, take exit 51 from Highway 19 and follow the signs.

COORDINATES ARE THE PROGRAMME MEETING POINT, NOT A STREET ADDRESS. The point recorded here is the meet-up location published in the operator's own page data for these programmes, and their instructions name the Nature House as that meeting point. It sits about 500 m from the single point the operator publishes for the park as a whole, which is 49.322571 and -124.26199, the same figure BC Parks uses to centre its own park map. The park point has not been used. A driver still needs the on-the-day directions, because the Nature House is reached on foot by trail from parking lot 1, from the campground or from the beach.
youngest age welcomed is not stated for the park or the Nature House. Jerry's Rangers publishes 5 to 12, but that is one programme's age band, not a rule about who is welcome.
no lead time, no chaperone expectation and no minimum group size are published for any of these programmes. The only group figure is a maximum of 25.
no duration is published for Jerry's Rangers or for the evening presentation. Only the nature walk gives an hour.
rain backup is not stated. All three programmes are outdoors and the one building on site is shut, so there is no published wet weather fallback.

step free and stroller access to the Nature House are not stated. The accessibility text on the operator's location page covers campsites, showers, flush toilets, beach access, many walking trails and day-use parking stalls, but says nothing about the trail to the Nature House or the building itself, so the field has been left blank rather than assumed. Detailed accessibility information is on a separate BC Parks accessibility site, which is off the operator's own domain and has not been read here.
bus parking is not stated. The programme page refers to parking lot 1 without saying what fits in it.

THE PROGRAMME IS LABELLED ENDED IN ONE PLACE AND OPEN IN ANOTHER. Their Discover Parks Ambassadors page shows Ended beside this programme, while the programme's own page carries no such label and shows Current status: Open under Location availability. The Open line appears to describe the park rather than the programme. Recorded as a conflict so a director sees both.

The park facilities, accessibility text and pet rules recorded here come from the operator's own Rathtrevor location page and from bcparks.ca, which is the park authority rather than the operator's own domain.

Both images recorded here were opened and looked at in a browser before their descriptions were written. The photo gallery lower down the shared nature house page is common to all four of the operator's nature houses, so only the section image sitting directly under the Rathtrevor heading was taken from it.

values: Now closed. See you in Summer 2027!
conflicts.note: Their own pages disagree about whether anything happens here. One says the nature house is shut until the summer of 2027. Their list of park programmes marks the free walks and children's sessions as finished, while the page for those same sessions says open and describes them meeting at that building. Worth settling with a phone call before you plan a trip out here.
